371561.title: Localised representation conjecture for string graphs on surfaces
371561.literal_statement: Let $\Sigma$ be a surface with Euler genus $g$, and let $G$ be a string graph in $\Sigma$. A string representation $\mathcal{C}$ of $G$ in $\Sigma$ assigns a non-self-intersecting curve to each vertex, with two curves intersecting exactly when the corresponding vertices are adjacent. **Localised representation conjecture.** There exists a function $f$ such that for every surface $\Sigma$ with Euler genus $g$ and every string graph $G$ in $\Sigma$, there is a string representation $\mathcal{C}$ of $G$ in $\Sigma$ such that, for each $u\in V(G)$, the curve representing $u$ is involved in at most $f(d_G(u),g)$ crossings. The planar case is established earlier in the paper, while the extension to arbitrary surfaces is presented as open and would yield bounded-degree consequences for string graphs on surfaces.

372361.title: Rounded upper-bound conjecture for distances from triangular tilings
372361.literal_statement:
Let $d(k)$ be the distance associated with the order-$k$ triangular tiling, and let $\alpha$ be the corresponding angle parameter. For $n\geq 1$ and $k\geq 7$, define the displayed rounded upper bound by 
$$
\left\lfloor\frac{\pi}{\alpha}n-\sqrt{\left(\frac{\pi}{\alpha}-1\right)\left(\frac{\pi}{\alpha}-3\right)n^2+6\left(\frac{\pi}{\alpha}-1\right)n-\frac{2\pi}{\alpha}+3}\right\rfloor.
$$
 **Rounded upper-bound conjecture.** For all $n\geq 1$ and all $k\geq 7$, 
$$
e_{d(k)}(n)=\left\lfloor\frac{\pi}{\alpha}n-\sqrt{\left(\frac{\pi}{\alpha}-1\right)\left(\frac{\pi}{\alpha}-3\right)n^2+6\left(\frac{\pi}{\alpha}-1\right)n-\frac{2\pi}{\alpha}+3}\right\rfloor.
$$
 This generalizes the analogous order-$7$ exact edge-count claim to all distances $d(k)$ with $k\geq 7$; the supplied text presents it as conjectural and gives no proof of equality.

362930.title: The converse Bernstein-coloring conjecture for independence in \(\mathcal{B}_{m,n}(d,d)\)
362930.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a bipartite graph, let $d\geq 0$ be an integer, and let $\mathcal{B}_{m,n}(d,d)$ denote the matroid introduced in the paper. A $d$-coloring of the edges of $G$ is **$d$-Bernstein** if it has no monochromatic cycles and there is a labeling $c\colon V(G)\to\mathbb{R}^d$, with $c(v)=(c_1(v),c_2(v),\dots,c_d(v))$, such that

$$
c_1(v)+c_2(v)+\cdots+c_d(v)=0
$$

for every $v\in V(G)$, and, for every edge $(u,v)\in E(G)$ with color $i$,

$$
c_i(u)+c_i(v)>c_j(u)+c_j(v)
$$

for every $j\in[d]\setminus\{i\}$. **The converse Bernstein-coloring conjecture.** If $G$ is independent in $\mathcal{B}_{m,n}(d,d)$, then $G$ admits a $d$-coloring that is $d$-Bernstein. This is presented as the converse to the preceding proposition, which proves that a $d$-Bernstein coloring implies independence in the relevant dual matroid; the supplied text gives no resolution status or further evidence, so the conjecture remains open.

363013.title: A polynomial sunflower conjecture for sparse vectors over finite cyclic groups
363013.literal_statement:
Let $p$ be a (not necessarily prime) integer and let $r\ge 1$. For integers $n,k,t\ge 1$, consider vectors $v_1,\ldots,v_k\in\mathbb{Z}_p^n$, each with at most $r$ non-zero coordinates.

**Polynomial sunflower conjecture.** There exist constants $c_1(p),c_2(p)>0$ such that whenever

$$
k\ge c_1(p)t^{c_2(p)},
$$

there are a subset $I\subset [k]$ of size $t$ and pairwise disjoint subsets $X_i\subset [n]$ for $i\in\{0\}\cup I$ such that, for every $i\in I$, the set of non-zero coordinates of $v_i$ is $X_0\cup X_i$, and the restrictions of $v_1,\ldots,v_k$ to the coordinates in $X_0$ coincide.

This is a variant of the sunflower conjecture for sparse vectors and would yield polynomial dependence on $\epsilon^{-1}$ in the relevant quantitative bounds. The paper presents it as an open question motivated by the sunflower conjecture of Erdős and Rado and recent progress toward that conjecture.
363013.mathematical_attempts: The source fixes p and r before existential constants, while naming them c1(p),c2(p). Under fixed-r dependence, ordinary colored sunflower estimates already give polynomial dependence on t; uniform-in-r reading has a generic obstruction from supports choosing one of each of r disjoint pairs (2^r distinct supports with no 3-sunflower). Neither observation establishes a substantive intended-source solution. No credit claimed for interpreting this notation defect.
363013.remaining_lemma_or_gap: Recover intended parameter dependence before investing; a uniformly r-independent assertion is incompatible with the elementary pair-choice family, while fixed-r polynomial bounds are classical.

363699.title: Ballantine--Burson--Craig--Folsom--Wen hook length bias conjecture for self-conjugate partitions
363699.literal_statement:
For each $n$, let $\mathcal{SC}(n)$ be the set of self-conjugate partitions of $n$, let $\mathcal{DO}(n)$ be the set of partitions of $n$ with distinct odd parts, and let $n_t(\lambda)$ denote the number of hooks of length $t$ in a partition $\lambda$. Define

$$
a_t^*(n):=\sum_{\lambda\in\mathcal{SC}(n)}n_t(\lambda),\qquad b_t^*(n):=\sum_{\lambda\in\mathcal{DO}(n)}n_t(\lambda).
$$

**Ballantine--Burson--Craig--Folsom--Wen hook length bias conjecture.** For every integer $t\geq 2$, both of the following hold:

1. There exists an integer $N_t^*$ such that $a_t^*(n)\geq b_t^*(n)$ for all $n>N_t^*$.
2. There exists a constant $\gamma_t^*>1$ such that

$$
\frac{a_t^*(n)}{b_t^*(n)}\longrightarrow\gamma_t^*
\quad\text{as }n\longrightarrow\infty.
$$

The conjecture formulates the eventual hook-length bias between self-conjugate partitions and partitions with distinct odd parts; the source says that Craig, Dawsey, and Han proved the corresponding conjecture, so both assertions are solved.

366413.title: The tight tree Ramsey growth conjecture for non-trivial tight hypergraph trees
366413.literal_statement:
Let $r\text{-graph}$ mean an $r$-uniform hypergraph. A tight $r$-tree is an $r$-graph whose edges can be ordered as $e_1,dots,e_t$ so that for every $i\geq 2$ there exist $v\in e_i$ and $1\leq s\leq i-1$ with $v\notin\bigcup_{j=1}^{i-1}e_j$ and $e_i\setminus\{v\}\subset e_s$. A tight $r$-tree is **non-trivial** if no vertex is contained in all of its edges. For an $r$-graph $F$, let $R(F,n)$ be the least integer $N$ such that every $F$-free $N$-vertex $r$-graph has an independent set of size $n$.

**Tight tree Ramsey growth conjecture.** For $r\geq 5$, if $T$ is a non-trivial tight $r$-tree, then there exist constants $c_1,c_2>0$ such that, for every positive integer $n$,

$$
c_1n^{r-1}\leq R(T,n)\leq c_2n^{r-1}.
$$

The paper proves this order of growth for $r=3$ and $r=4$. The conjecture extends that result to all higher uniformities; the source notes that natural generalizations of the known constructions already fail for $r=5$, so the lower bound remains the main obstacle.
366413.review_depth: Conjecture 1; Theorem 1.1; Proposition 2.2; concluding failed r=5 constructions
366413.mathematical_attempts: This is an asymptotic Ramsey growth problem despite its finite metadata cues. Source proves the upper bound for all r and lower bound for r=3,4; the lower bound for arbitrary nontrivial tight r-trees with r>=5 remains the hard component. Small Ramsey values cannot refute unspecified positive constants.

359365.title: The branched-cover conjecture for Garland posets
359365.literal_statement:
Let $k>0$. A finite cubical poset $Q$ has dimension $k+1$, and every $k$-face of $Q$ is contained in at least $d$ facets. A **$k$-branched cover** is a branched cover with branching in the sense used for Garland posets.

**Branched-cover conjecture.** For every $k>0$ there is $d$ such that, whenever $Q$ is a finite cubical poset of dimension $k+1$ and every $k$-face is contained in at least $d$ facets, there is a pair of $k$-branched covers

$$
Q \leftarrow P \rightarrow R
$$

such that the Garland poset of $R$ satisfies the hypotheses of the cubical Garland result.

The conjecture proposes a way to overcome the fact that passing to covers can enlarge the spectrum of link graphs and thereby invalidate the required spectral hypothesis. The preceding discussion explains that suitable branched covers can be made $k$-monodromy-free; what remains conjectural is the existence of the pair of covers with the stated Garland property.

359534.title: Robust exact-threshold conjecture for Hamilton cycle embeddings
359534.literal_statement:
For $k\in\mathbb N$, $d\in[k-1]$, $\ell\in\{0,\dots,k-1\}$, and $n$ divisible by $k-\ell$, let $h_{k,\ell,d}(n)$ be the least integer $D\geq0$ such that every $n$-vertex $k$-uniform hypergraph $H$ with $\delta_d(H)\geq D$ contains a Hamilton $\ell$-cycle. Let $C_{n,k,\ell}$ denote that cycle, and call a distribution on its embeddings **vertex-spread** when it satisfies the paper's vertex-spread condition. **Robust exact-threshold conjecture.** For every $k\in\mathbb N$, there exists $C=C(k)$ such that, for every $d\in[k-1]$, $\ell\in\{0,\dots,k-1\}$, and admissible $n$, every $n$-vertex $k$-uniform hypergraph $H$ with

$$
\delta_d(H)\geq h_{k,\ell,d}(n)
$$

has a $(C/n)$-vertex-spread distribution on embeddings $C_{n,k,\ell}\hookrightarrow H$.
This is a robust strengthening of the exact Hamilton-cycle threshold statement. The source presents it as open, although it records some special cases where the underlying exact threshold is known.

359866.title: Polychromatic finiteness conjecture for hereditary hypergraph families
359866.literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal F$ be a hereditary family of hypergraphs, and let $m_k(\mathcal F)$ be the least integer $m$, if it exists, such that every $m$-heavy member of $\mathcal F$ is polychromatically $k$-colorable; set $m_k(\mathcal F)=\infty$ if no such $m$ exists. A hypergraph is $m$-heavy when every edge has size at least $m$, and a coloring is polychromatic when every edge contains a vertex of each of the $k$ colors.

**Polychromatic finiteness conjecture.** If $m_2(\mathcal F)<\infty$, then $m_k(\mathcal F)<\infty$ for every $k$ for any hereditary family $\mathcal F$.

This conjecture is known when $m_2(\mathcal F)=2$, by a result of Berge, but remains open in general. It asks whether finiteness of the threshold for 2-colorability forces finiteness of the corresponding threshold for every number of colors.

359867.title: Keszegh–Pálvölgyi linear bound conjecture for polychromatic coloring
359867.literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal F$ be a hereditary family of hypergraphs, and let $m_k(\mathcal F)$ be the least integer $m$, if it exists, such that every $m$-heavy member of $\mathcal F$ is polychromatically $k$-colorable; set $m_k(\mathcal F)=\infty$ if no such $m$ exists. A hypergraph is $m$-heavy when every edge has size at least $m$, and a coloring is polychromatic when every edge contains a vertex of each of the $k$ colors.

**Keszegh–Pálvölgyi linear bound conjecture.** For every $k$ and every hereditary family $\mathcal F$,

$$
m_k(\mathcal F)\le (k-1)(m_2(\mathcal F)-1)+1.
$$

This is a stronger quantitative form of the finiteness conjecture and was conjectured by Keszegh and the author. The paper states that it is disproved by a 5-uniform hypergraph with no polychromatic 3-coloring, although all its restricted subhypergraphs with edges of size at least 3 are 2-colorable.

382196.title: Filtered combinatorial invariance conjecture for Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials
382196.literal_statement:
Let $(W,S)$ be a finite Coxeter system equipped with a canonical filtration

$$
\underline{J}^0=(\emptyset=J_0\subsetneq J_1\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq J_r=S).
$$

This filtration gives a reflection-coloring map $\alpha:T\to\{1,\ldots,r\}$ by assigning to each reflection the least $i$ such that it lies in $W_{J_i}$. **Filtered combinatorial invariance conjecture.** For any finite Coxeter system, there is an assigned canonical filtration $\underline{J}^0$ such that, for two filtered finite Coxeter systems and an isomorphism $\phi$ of their directed Bruhat intervals, if there is an increasing map $\gamma:\{1,\ldots,r_1\}\to\{1,\ldots,r_2\}$ satisfying

$$
\gamma\circ\alpha_1(t)=\alpha_2(t')
$$

for every edge $\sigma_1\leq z<tz\leq\omega_1$, where $t'\in W_2$ is the reflection determined by $\phi(tz)=t'\phi(z)$, then

$$
P_{\sigma_1,\omega_1}=P_{\sigma_2,\omega_2}.
$$

The conjecture refines combinatorial invariance by requiring preservation of reflection colors up to an increasing relabeling. Its status is not specified in the supplied text.

354345.title: The classification conjecture for transversals in group subsquares
354345.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a group and let $A,B\subseteq G$ satisfy $|A|=|B|=n$. A **subsquare** $A\times B$ is the corresponding subarray of the multiplication table, and a **transversal** meets every row, column, and symbol exactly once. **Classification conjecture.** For all $n$, $A\times B$ has a transversal unless there exist $k\geq1$, $g_1,g_2\in G$, and a subgroup $H\subseteq G$ such that either:

1. $H$ does not satisfy the Hall–Paige condition, $A\cong g_1H$, and $B\cong Hg_2$; or
2. $H\cong(\mathbb{Z}_2)^k$, and

$$
g_1A\cong H\setminus\{a_1,a_2\},\qquad g_2B\cong H\setminus\{b_1,b_2\},
$$

for distinct $a_1,a_2\in H$ and distinct $b_1,b_2\in H$ satisfying $a_1+a_2+b_1+b_2=0$. This is proposed as an extension of the paper's large-$n$ classification theorem and is not given a resolution in the supplied text.

355361.title: The Hadamard-closure conjecture for the subalgebra of a Q-polynomial graph
355361.literal_statement:
Let $\Gamma=(X,\mathcal R)$ be a finite, undirected, connected graph without loops or multiple edges, with diameter $D\geq 1$, and let $A$ be its adjacency matrix. An ordering $\{V_i\}_{i=0}^d$ of the eigenspaces of $A$ is **Q-polynomial** if

$$
\sum_{\ell=0}^i V_\ell=\sum_{\ell=0}^i (V_1)^{\circ \ell}\qquad (0\leq i\leq d).
$$

The graph $\Gamma$ is Q-polynomial if it has at least one such ordering. Let $M$ be the subalgebra of $\operatorname{Mat}_X(\mathbb R)$ generated by $A$. **Hadamard-closure conjecture.** If $\Gamma$ is Q-polynomial, then

$$
B\circ C\in M
$$

for all $B,C\in M$. This would extend a central closure property of the subconstituent algebra from distance-regular graphs to the broader class of Q-polynomial graphs, whose distance-regularity is not assumed here; the conjecture's status is not determined in the source.

356719.title: Strict hierarchy conjecture for polynomial partition regularity
356719.literal_statement: For $d\geq 1$, let $P_d$ be the set of polynomials in countably many variables with nonnegative integer coefficients, constant term, and degree at most $d$ in each variable. A pattern is **partition regular** over $P_d$ if every finite coloring of $P_d$ contains a monochromatic realization of the pattern, and it **appears** in $P_i$ if its one-coloring contains a monochromatic copy of $P_i$. **Strict hierarchy conjecture.** For all $1\leq i<j$, there exists a pattern $\mathcal{F}$ such that $\mathcal{F}$ is partition regular in $P_j$ but not in $P_i$, while $\mathcal{F}$ appears in $P_i$. This proposes that partition regularity over the bounded-degree polynomial settings has genuinely distinct levels; the paper gives the conjecture as complementary to the non-partition-regularity conjecture for $\{x,y,x+y,xy\}$, and no general resolution is supplied.

357064.title: General factorization conjecture for cyclic block partitions
357064.literal_statement:
Fix an ordered set partition $\mathbf{S}=(S_1,\ldots,S_k)$ of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ into $k$ cyclically contiguous interval blocks. Let $d$ be the number of blocks with size at least $2$, and let $\mathcal{N}_{\mathbf{S}}$ denote the associated set of distinct nonzero kinematic blades.

**Block-partition factorization conjecture.** There is an ordering $(\mathbf{T}_1,\ldots,\mathbf{T}_{(d-1)(k-1)-1},\mathbf{S})$ with $\{\mathbf{T}_1,\ldots,\mathbf{T}_{(d-1)(k-1)-1}\}=\mathcal{N}_{\mathbf{S}}$ such that the iterated residue is nonzero and

$$
\operatorname{Res}_{\eta_{(\mathbf{T}_{(d-1)(k-1)-1})}=0}\!\left(\cdots\operatorname{Res}_{\eta_{(\mathbf{T}_1)}=0}\!\left(\operatorname{Res}_{\eta_{(\mathbf{S})}=0}(m^{(k)}_n)\right)\cdots\right)=\prod_{\ell=1}^{d}m^{(k)}_{n_\ell},
$$

under a suitable identification of kinematic parameters, where $n_1+\cdots+n_d=n+d(k-1)$.

This extends the explicit factorization proposal to arbitrary $k$ and block degeneracies. The supplied text gives no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.

382034.title: Minimal-weight-vector conjecture for tight irreducible subcube partitions
382034.literal_statement:
A **subcube partition** $F$ of length $n$ has weight vector $w(F)=(w_0,\ldots,w_n)$, where $w_h$ is the number of subcubes containing $h$ entries equal to $1$. For $h\leq n$, write $w_{\geq h}=w_h+\cdots+w_n$. A weight vector **majorizes** another if all corresponding upper-tail sums are at least as large. The partition is **tight** if every coordinate is constrained by some subcube and **irreducible** if no proper subset of more than one subcube has a union that is a subcube.

**Minimal-weight-vector conjecture.** For every $n\geq 3$, the minimal weight vectors, under majorization, of tight irreducible subcube partitions of length $n$ are

$$
(1,n-1,n-1,0,\ldots,0)
$$

and

$$
(1,n,n-3,1,0,\ldots,0).
$$

These two vectors are realized by explicit constructions in the paper; whether they are the only minimal vectors in general remains open.

368808.title: Buratti-Horak-Rosa conjecture on edge lengths of Hamiltonian paths
368808.literal_statement:
Let $[n]=\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$ denote the vertices of a circulant instance, and let edge length $i$ refer to the corresponding circulant edge-length class, for $i=1,\ldots,d$. Let $t_1,t_2,\ldots,t_d$ be nonnegative integers, where $t_i$ counts the edges of length $i$.

**Buratti-Horak-Rosa conjecture.** If

$$
\sum_{i=1}^d t_i=n-1
$$

and, for every divisor $q$ of $n$,

$$
\sum_{1\leq i\leq d:\,q\mid i}t_i\leq n-q,
$$

then there exists a Hamiltonian path on $[n]$ using exactly $t_i$ edges of length $i$ for each $i=1,\ldots,d$.

The conjecture characterizes the combinations of edge lengths that can occur in a Hamiltonian path and asserts that the divisibility inequalities are the only obstruction. Its prime-order case was conjectured by Buratti in the 2000s; the supplied text gives no evidence that the full conjecture has been resolved.

Generic circulant obstructions and credited order-15 monophonic-position result do not settle BHR. Historical alias 354609, r142, subsequently found and route stopped.
